title: Pay for substation outages and limit them per region

expected.says: Run's report for the tiny fleet matches the expected report

blueprint.signature: def build(fleet: list[Transformer], request: Request) -> Built
blueprint.contract: As before, and when the request has outages (an outage_cost above 0 or an outages limit; Request.has_outages() answers it): one binary out[s, year] per candidate substation and plan year, named `out_<s>_<year>`; a row `outage_<s>_<year>` allowing replacements at s in that year only when out[s, year] is 1 (the sum of its candidates' x at most their count times out); when request.outages is set, a row `coord_<region>_<year>` for each region with candidate substations, keeping the region's outages within it; and request.outage_cost times each year's outages in that year's budget row. Built.out holds the outage variables, keyed by (substation, year), and is empty without outages.
blueprint.idea: A cost shared by several decisions gets its own binary, linked to the decisions that need it, and is paid from the budget row rather than scored in the objective.

blueprint.signature: def outages(fleet: list[Transformer], replace: dict[str, int]) -> set[tuple[str, int]]
blueprint.contract: The (substation, year) pairs a plan's replacements need: one per substation and year with at least one replacement.
blueprint.idea: An outage serves every replacement at its substation that year.

blueprint.signature: def spend_by_year(fleet: list[Transformer], replace: dict[str, int], outage_cost: int = 0) -> dict[int, int]
blueprint.contract: Each year's replacement cost plus outage_cost for each outage that year, $k, by year in order.
blueprint.idea: The report counts money the way the budget row does, each outage once.

cases: one outage serves every replacement at its substation that year
the plan bundles replacements at one substation to pay for one outage
a region's outage limit holds even when outages cost nothing
the report's spend counts each outage once
